observations.title: logs/attempt1-runner-stdout.log is not a faithful UTF-8/LF copy (UTF-16LE with BOM, blank lines inserted)
observations.detail: The committed copy is UTF-16LE with BOM (FF FE) and every original line is followed by an empty line (raw 183 lines -> 366 committed lines; the delivery record says 367). This contradicts README §10.4 and the delivery record evidence_format.line_endings ('all evidence text files UTF-8 without BOM, LF/CR=0'). The content is readable as UTF-16 and the numbers are unaffected (facts/samples/guards are the authoritative sources), but the line count in the record does not match the decoded text.
observations.fix_or_accept: FIX: re-export as UTF-8 without BOM, LF, no inserted blank lines, then update the delivery record sha/bytes/lines and the evidence_format statement. ACCEPT only if the entry is explicitly recorded as an encoding exception (the current declaration would still be wrong).

observations.title: The spike timing statement 'about 0.7 s after launcher exit' is not supported by the artifacts
observations.detail: The runner writes each entity log after the process ends (script line 253 then ENTITY_DONE line 256), so the launcher log mtime 17:03:36.808 is at or after the launcher exit. The spike sample is 2026-10-27T17:03:36.7225390, i.e. 86 ms BEFORE that log write; the stage2 start is bounded at 17:03:37.658..38.443, so the spike is at least 0.9 s before stage2. The defensible wording is 'at the launcher exit/log-write boundary (about +-0.1 s), before the stage2 start'. The attribution direction (launcher NVRTC/cuModule teardown) and its inference status are unchanged.
observations.fix_or_accept: FIX: update README §10.2, window-receipt budget_deviation.attribution.basis and the receipt attempt1 block to the boundary wording. ACCEPT: peak value, seq, timestamp and attribution direction do not change.
